findings.message: `appUsable` turns every failure to read the credential into `false` with `.catch(() => false)`. That includes a KMS outage (SecretsUnavailableError), a refused use (ForbiddenError), an expiry and any other error. So 'could not check' is reported as 'the stored value is unusable'. The result is then cached in the module-level map until the credential is next rotated. `githubAppStatus` reports `incomplete: true`, Integrations shows 'Incomplete · set it up again', and chat offers 'Set up the GitHub app' instead of Rotate/Remove. Fix: catch only the parse result. Rethrow, or return 'unknown', for errors from `useSecret` itself (the status can show the existing unavailable wording through `asRefusal`). Never cache a failed read. Only a value that was actually parsed should be stored. Add a test where the KMS is unavailable for the first status read and later recovers.
findings.scenario: The KMS is briefly unreachable when an Admin first opens /settings/integrations after the app was set up with a valid `id:secret`. useSecret throws SecretsUnavailableError, which is cached as false for `tenant:rotatedAt`. The KMS comes back, but the chip still says 'Incomplete · set it up again' and chat still suggests 'Set up the GitHub app' until someone rewrites a credential that was valid all along.

findings.message: The fake GitHub returns `incorrect_client_credentials` for the magic code `wrongsecret`, whatever client_id or client_secret is sent. So the AC-2 test never stores a wrong secret and drives it through the exchange; it plants the refusal by the code value. Make the fake return `incorrect_client_credentials` whenever `client_id`/`client_secret` don't match `app-id`/`app-secret-fake-…`. Then the test can store a well-formed but wrong secret (and a wrong client id) and connect with `good`.
findings.scenario: A regression that sends the wrong secret field, or drops client_secret, still passes the AC-2 test, because the fake answers by `code` alone.

findings.message: The `usable` cache is a process-wide Map that never evicts. Every rotation adds a new `tenant:rotatedAt` key, so it grows without limit across tenants and rotations. The `has`-then-`await`-then-`set` sequence also lets concurrent status reads (the chip and every Integrations chat-suggestion `when`) each do an audited secret use before the first one lands. Keep one entry per tenant (replace the entry when rotatedAt changes) and store the in-flight promise so concurrent reads share it.
findings.scenario: Integrations loads, and the page's status read plus two `admin()` suggestion checks run concurrently on a cold cache. That gives three audited 'GitHub app check' uses instead of one.

findings.message: AC-2 maps the token-exchange errors an Admin must fix to their own results. Its test checks a single case, `incorrect_client_credentials`. Replace it with a table over the exchange's error replies, e.g. `incorrect_client_credentials` → credentials, `redirect_uri_mismatch` → callback, and `bad_verification_code` → github (still 'Try again'). Each row should go through `completeGitHubConnect`. As written, the test can't catch a mapping that sends a credentials error to `github`, or a change that also sends `bad_verification_code` to credentials.
findings.scenario: Change `resultCodeOf` so it checks `isGitHubReplyError` before `isGitHubCredentialsError`, and make `GitHubCredentialsError` extend `GitHubReplyError`. A wrong secret then shows 'Try again'. The single-case test only catches this if that exact ordering breaks it, and nothing guards the neighbouring mappings.
